title: New Orleans versus Chicago musicians and Dave Peyton at the Regal
summary: He saw no division between locals and New Orleans players and mentions working for Dave Peyton at the Regal after Tate.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did you work -- well, let me -- some people have done some research, and have looked up old columns that were written by one of the big band leaders on Southside in the twenties, Dave Peyton, maybe, wrote a column for The Defender.

And it seems like there were like three divisions of musicians on the Southside, those who played in the theaters, and those who played in ballrooms, and those who played in what they called cabarets. And some

of his columns, he puts down the guys who were playing in cabarets, a lot of the New Orleans musicians. There seemed to be some bad feeling between the established Chicago musicians and the guys coming up from New Orleans. Were you aware of any of that?
No, I wasn't. I worked with Dave Peyton at the Regal Theater.
That was when I left Erskine Tate. I just came across the street to the Regal.
Well, you've worked and recorded with a lot of the musicians who came from New Orleans, like the Dodds Brothers. You worked with Jimmy Noone, I believe.
Did they operate differently from the guys who, you know, were from Chicago? I mean, were they harder to work for, easier to work for, or --
No, I didn't see any difference.
